owner: MES-104 (C1b-i). C1a's (MES-97) 18 client rows were MOVED here unchanged.
what_this_is: The AUTHORED adjudications for the CLIENT leg — one record per (ET-CC member, claim, OC check). Judgements are data with evidence; derivations are code. `oc_key`, `shape` and `bucket` appear NOWHERE here: the generator derives them through MCP.Conformance.MatchKey and refuses any edge whose stored form disagrees.
why_one_file_per_leg: PM composition ruling on MES-104 (comment 28287). C1a's file declared 21 members, 18 of them client, so C1b-i could not declare the client leg without deciding what happened to the overlap: leaving it would make G15a red in both files. The 18 moved here, `crosswalk-edges.json` re-declared to its 3 non-client rows, and `--edges` became repeatable. C1b-ii and C1b-iii APPEND to this file; C1c (MES-105) absorbs the residual one.

the_population_this_file_declares.rule: Every ET-CC member B2b attributes to the CLIENT leg that is either in CG7 — C1b-i's slice — or was already adjudicated by C1a (a token, or a contradicts_oc record). NOTHING outside it is adjudicated here.

selector.what_this_is: The EXECUTABLE half of `rule`. The generator evaluates it against the source named below and requires the result to be SET-EQUAL, in both directions, to the population this file derives. Prose only becomes a guard when something can run it.
selector.why_it_must_name_a_file_other_than_this_: C1a derived its declared population by unioning the register_keys the edges file itself carried, so a dropped row did not violate the universe, it SHRANK it — measured on MES-99, both a dropped edge and a dropped declared_unmatched row built cleanly at 20 members with every set comparison still exact. A selector that read this file's own rows would be circular by another route.
selector.denotes: 45 ET-CC members: the 29 B2b attributes to the CLIENT leg and CG7 — C1b-i's own slice — plus the 18 client members C1a had already adjudicated, whose rows moved here under the PM's composition ruling. The two sets overlap in exactly 2 members (the CG7 rows C1a already carried a token for), which is why 29 + 18 is 45 and not 47.
selector.why_the_cg_conjunct_and_not_the_whole_cl: MES-104 was re-scoped to C1b-i = CG7 at the plan hop. The other 62 client members are C1b-ii's (CG1 + CG2 + CG4) and C1b-iii's (the 55 with no CG), and the assertion that the three sub-populations UNION to all 107 lands on C1b-iii, the last of them — not here.

the_population_this_file_declares.everything_else_is: not_yet_adjudicated — a THIRD state, distinct from bucket 1 ('we looked, there is no counterpart') and from A3 §6 state 4 ('nobody has adjudicated this member'). The 62 client members outside it are C1b-ii's and C1b-iii's; the server leg and the 29 none_determinable are C1c's.

the_check_population_this_file_declares.rule: The 29 in-denominator OC checks A4 assigns to CG7. This file is total over them: every one is axis-decomposed, and every one either carries an edge or is reported in bucket 2 by name.

selector.what_this_is: The check half of the declaration, and the reason bucket 2 can now be non-empty. C1a derived its check population from the tags its own edges carried, so bucket 2 — the complement of the edge-bearing checks within it — was EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and its `CHECKED, AND ZERO` was a vacuous truth. Declaring the checks from outside the file is what makes the question answerable.
selector.source_owner: MES-97 (C1a) — `mix conformance.locator`'s output, one row per in-denominator check
selector.denotes: The 29 in-denominator OC checks A4 assigns to CG7 — `http-custom-headers` 18 + `http-invalid-tool-headers` 11 (cg-reconciliation.md §4's scenario table). The selector names the SCENARIOS rather than the 29 tokens, so a check added to either scenario by a harness bump joins the population instead of being silently outside it.
selector.why_the_locator_artefact_and_not_A1s_man: A1's manifest nests its checks under scenarios and its key is a six-field LIST; the selector's `key_field` must name a string field, and refuses anything else rather than stringifying it. The locator artefact is flat, carries one row per in-denominator check, and already carries the TOKEN — which is the field the edges in this file address checks by, so the two sides are compared in the same unit.

the_check_population_this_file_declares.checks_addressed_outside_it: The 18 moved C1a rows address 11 client checks in `request-metadata`, `sep-2322-client-request-state` and `tools_call`. Those are ADDRESSED but not DECLARED: they carry inherited edges and take no part in bucket 2, because the rest of their scenarios has not been adjudicated and reporting their siblings as 'no ET counterpart' would assert of each something nobody has looked at. C1b-iii declares those scenarios.
the_check_population_this_file_declares.the_bound_this_leaves: A file could declare a small check population, address many checks outside it, and report a flattering bucket 2. What stops that here is not the arithmetic: it is that the selector names an EXTERNAL anchor by scenario, that every declared check must be axis-decomposed before it counts (the generator refuses otherwise), and that the checks addressed outside are enumerated above rather than left silent. Stated as a residual, not papered over.

what_a_record_carries_and_why.member: MES-67's unit: module AND test name. The `register_key` is docs/conformance/etcc-row-key.md §1's key and is what joins this file to the register; it was extracted from the register, never typed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.claim: A3 §1's atom of matching — finer than a test, coarser than an assert. A member bundling claims contributes several edges and they are never collapsed.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.tag: A3 §5's token. The generator DECODES and RESOLVES it against A1's manifest and derives the six-field oc_key from the resolution; it never accepts a key from this file.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.axes: One verdict per axis of the check's predicate, naming axes that must exist in the check's axis decomposition (A3's 13 or C1's 11). The generator refuses an axis name the decomposition does not contain — a verdict against an axis nobody extracted is a verdict about nothing.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.et_verdict: The member's own run verdict. Every member of this population is `green`: re-measured at 42e6b19 over the full suite, all 281 ET-CC members pass. So buckets 3 (green OC / red ET) and 6 (red in both) are EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION on this data — checked, and zero, with the predicate recorded.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.evidence: File, line and the assertion, for every axis verdict. Ruling 7: an address is not evidence, the bytes at it are.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.not_carried: No `oc_key`, no `shape`, no `bucket`, no OC verdict. All four are derived — the OC verdict from A1's committed per-check `status` at the accepted run, the rest through MatchKey.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.the_search_that_found_none: On every declared_unmatched record C1b-i authored: what was read, and what it said. A verdict of 'no counterpart' with no search behind it is a silence wearing a token (A2d). C1a's five inherited records predate this field and do not carry it — stated rather than backfilled, since backfilling would be inventing the search.
what_a_record_carries_and_why.why_no_counterpart: Which of the two reason-slugs applies and why. `no-oc-scenario` — the suite has no such check ANYWHERE, so the search is over all 173. `no-oc-fixture-case` — the scenario exists and is matched, but its fixture holds no case that would exercise the constraint, so the search is over the fixture.

how_a_silent_axis_was_decided: Conservatively, and the rule is stated rather than applied case by case: a claim counts as covering an axis only when an assertion's SUBJECT is the behaviour that axis names. A test asserting a tool's RESULT does not cover an axis about the ARGUMENTS' wire type, and a test asserting that a capability is ABSENT does not cover an axis about the SHAPE of a present one. This is match-relation.md §6's CG5 rule — a mention is not a discharge — turned on our own side of the relation. Where it was a judgement rather than a reading, the edge's `evidence` says so in those words.
the_all_silent_case: Four edges have EVERY axis silent. They are recorded and ESCALATED, never bucketed. A3 §2 rules that covering zero of one axis 'is no match, not a partial one'; generalised to N axes that is exactly this case, and A3 §3's table has no row for it — `shape_from_axes/1` would call it `:partial` and bucket 5 would swallow it. Dropping the edges instead would be worse: the member would then look edge-less and therefore bucket-1, asserting 'we looked and there is no counterpart' where the truth is 'there is a counterpart and our claim does not touch its predicate'. Escalation is A3 §7's own mechanism for a case the rule does not decide.
what_unmatched_means_in_a_file_that_decl: A3 §6 state 3 reads absolutely — the member has NO OC counterpart. In a file whose check population is a declared subset it can only mean 'no counterpart among the checks this file declares', and the difference is not pedantic: two CG7 members assert a claim whose counterpart exists in CG1's `http-standard-headers`, which is C1b-ii's. Those claims are recorded under `claims_without_an_edge` with the counterpart named and C1b-ii as owner, so the record says which kind of absence it is rather than collapsing the two.
claims_without_an_edge_note: A3's state 3 is a property of a MEMBER, and a member is either edge-bearing or declared unmatched — the generator's bucket-1 reconciliation requires exactly that. So a member that matches on some claims and not on others has nowhere to put the unmatched ones, and C1b-i found six. They are recorded here with the search that found none and ESCALATED rather than dropped: dropping them would report the member as fully matched, and filing a second record would make the member both edge-bearing and bucket 1. Whether A3 §6 should gain a claim-level state 3 is the PM's, not this file's.
